faithfulness_cross_check.description: Tester independently re-ran this cross-check (not taken on faith from impl-notes.md): loaded the real vllm_ascend.eplb.core.policy.policy_default_eplb.DefaultEplb standalone from instances/vllm-ascend/source (stubbing the vllm_ascend/.../policy parent packages in sys.modules to dodge vllm_ascend/__init__.py's torch/CANN-importing chain -- policy_default_eplb.py itself only imports numpy/collections/typing + policy_abstract, which has zero third-party deps) and ran it side by side with implementation/eplb.py.
faithfulness_cross_check.worked_example_result: Tester-verified by hand and by direct execution: on the chapter's exact 2-rank x 8-expert worked example, DefaultEplb().rebalance_experts and eplb.rebalance_experts return bit-for-bit identical output -- change=1, priority=[0], new_placement=[[[3, 4, 1, 7, 5], [0, 4, 6, 3, 2]]] on both sides (not just weight-equal; the literal card/slot assignment matches).
faithfulness_cross_check.fuzz_result: Tester re-ran an independent randomized cross-check (rng seed 7, 500 attempted trials / 178 valid after filtering for evenly-divisible slot counts; 2-5 cards, redundancy 0..cards-1, random workloads): 0/178 mismatches on change gate outcome AND exact new_placement (stronger than impl-notes' claimed weight-multiset-only agreement -- placements matched exactly, not just per-card totals).
faithfulness_cross_check.known_harmless_divergence: impl-notes.md flags a theoretical tie-break divergence risk (equal-weight cold experts landing on different cards between the two implementations' argsort ties); tester's fuzz run found no actual occurrence of this across 178 trials, consistent with both implementations using the identical np.argsort(..., kind='stable') tie-breaking rule.

notes: kind=primer per dossier: gate is lint_paper_grounding.py --expect-primer (no BLOCKING), not lint_fidelity.py -- implementation/eplb.py is a paper-faithful small reference port (NumPy, no torch), not a subtract-only companion. All 8 dossier mechanisms have either a direct test or an explicit, justified test-exemption (hierarchical-vs-global-policy: nothing implemented, matching both paper and landing code).
